subject: Engelska
title: Grammar: tenses
sourceSummary: Present simple versus present continuous, past simple, and expressing the future with "going to" and "will" — the basics before upper-secondary school builds on them.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: "She ___ to school every day."
questions.opener: Habits and routines are expressed with present simple — and third person singular (he/she/it) takes -s.
questions.explanation: Everyday routines are expressed in present simple. With "she" (third person singular), -s is added to the verb: "walks".

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: "Look! It ___ outside right now."
questions.opener: Something happening right at this moment — which tense is used then?
questions.explanation: "Right now" signals that something is happening at this moment — that requires present continuous: is/am/are + verb-ing.

questions.opener: Routines don't take the -ing form, even if it "feels" ongoing.
choices: I usually am eating breakfast at seven.
I usually eat breakfast at seven.
I usually eats breakfast at seven.
I am usually eat breakfast at seven.
questions.explanation: "Usually" signals a habit — that requires present simple without -ing. "I" does not take an -s (that is only added for he/she/it).

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: "We ___ to the cinema last Friday."
questions.opener: "Last Friday" points to a completed event in the past.
questions.explanation: "Last Friday" is a clear past-time expression that requires past simple. "Go" is irregular: go → went (not "goed").

questions.prompt: Choose the correct negative form: "She ___ finish her homework yesterday."
questions.opener: In negative sentences in the past, the helping verb "did" is used — and then the main verb stays in its base form.
questions.explanation: Negative past tense is formed with "didn't" + verb in the base form: "didn't finish", not "didn't finished" (double inflection is a common mistake).

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "I've already decided — I ___ study medicine after school."
questions.opener: A decision that has already been made is usually expressed with "going to", not "will".
questions.explanation: "Going to" is used for plans and decisions that have already been made. "Will" fits better for spontaneous decisions or promises made in the moment.

questions.prompt: Correct the three tense errors: "Every day I am walking to school. Yesterday I go by bus because it rain a lot. Tomorrow I will going by bike."
questions.opener: Three tenses are mixed up here: a routine, a completed event, and a future plan.
questions.answer: Every day I walk to school. Yesterday I went by bus because it rained a lot. Tomorrow I will go by bike.
steps: "I am walking" (routine, "every day") → "I walk". Habits take present simple, not continuous.
"Yesterday I go" → "Yesterday I went". "Yesterday" requires past simple; "go" is irregular: go → went.
"it rain a lot" → "it rained a lot". Regular verb in the past: rain → rained (-ed).
"I will going" → "I will go". After "will", the verb always stays in its base form, never with -ing.

questions.prompt: When do you use present simple, present continuous, past simple and "going to"/"will"?
questions.answer: Present simple: habits and routines (I play football every week). Present continuous: something happening right now (I am playing football right now). Past simple: completed events in the past, often with time expressions like yesterday/last week (I played football yesterday). Going to: plans and decisions already made (I'm going to play tomorrow). Will: spontaneous decisions, promises and predictions made in the moment (I think it will rain).
